riskDimensions.impactEvidence: A same-repository screenshot job has contents:write; the image job has packages:write. The patch supplies that full job token to a broader dependency-install process tree.
riskDimensions.likelihoodMeaning: The missing process-isolation property is established by source, not a numerical estimate of malicious-dependency occurrence. Actual abuse occurrence is unknown.
riskDimensions.protectionEvidence: 22 top-level installer tests exercise installer/file/HTTP/redirect/error behavior; none references the affected shared action or caller workflow files. This review ran no tests.
riskDimensions.recoveryEvidence: Candidate not merged by this task; no migrations or persisted data change required. Change credential inputs/callers while retaining installer implementation and release responsibilities.
riskDimensions.confidenceScope: Exact immutable candidate/base source and three concrete entry paths verified; no claim of exhaustive audit of every workflow or actual stolen token.

findings.evidence: The pnpm install --frozen-lockfile step unconditionally assigns FFMPEG_GITHUB_TOKEN from github.token, with no optional input.
findings.recipientBoundary: The pnpm process and allowed dependency lifecycle descendants receive this environment. The fixed-host rules of one FFmpeg HTTP function do not constrain other lifecycle processes.
findings.strongestCounterexample: An otherwise allowed ordinary lifecycle reads the new FFMPEG_GITHUB_TOKEN environment value in a caller whose token has write permissions. This is a source data-flow example, not executed exfiltration.
findings.legitimateControl: Default absent/empty optional credential; explicit input supplied only by confirmed read-token callers. Keep the existing allowBuilds and frozen lockfile.

findings.before: Exact same screenshots source existed at prior1ffa; checkout uses persist-credentials:false and explicit GITHUB_TOKEN appears only in the later evidence-publication step.
findings.after: The unchanged shared-action call now injects the full contents-write job token into pnpm installation due to the changed action.
findings.scope: Same-repository PR condition and existing path filters remain; this review does not claim the screenshots job ran in CI42590712093.
findings.minimalRepair: Do not opt this caller into the new credential input; retain its existing later publishing step and contents:write permission.

findings.before: Prior Dockerfile runs pnpm without a token secret. Current .dockerignore excludes .git, so host checkout credentials are not copied into this build context.
findings.after: Workflow injects github.token into FFMPEG_GITHUB_TOKEN and passes a BuildKit secret; Docker RUN maps the secret to environment for the complete pnpm install.
findings.secretMountBoundary: Optional BuildKit secret avoids an ARG or durable ENV entry, but does not downgrade token permissions or restrict it to only one child process in that RUN.
findings.minimalRepair: Remove the image workflow's automatic write-token env/--secret handoff. Keep anonymous install and the optional Docker secret declaration for explicit supported callers. Preserve package publishing later in the job.

findings.evidence: The host also calls the now-injecting shared action. However, image checkout does not set persist-credentials:false, so this review does not claim no Git credential was reachable by host dependencies before the patch.
findings.increment: The new automatic environment recipient path is real. The stronger newly crossed boundary is the Docker install process described separately.
findings.minimalRepair: The shared action default-none also removes this new environment injection, without claiming to solve every pre-existing CI credential channel.

facts: Only the dedicated FFMPEG_GITHUB_TOKEN is read at the pinned API fallback; no implicit generic GITHUB_TOKEN fallback.
Authorization is added only for the fixed API source's exact first HTTPS request; every redirect rebuilds headers and receives no credential.
Fixed sources, three redirects, 30-second per-attempt budget, bundle checksums and closed diagnostics remain part of the existing implementation.
These controls protect the installer HTTP sink and its logging; they do not remove credentials from siblings in the installation process tree.

minimalChangeBoundary.sharedAction: Add explicit optional credential input with default empty; environment references only that input, never github.token fallback.
minimalChangeBoundary.readCallers: Explicitly opt in only at reviewed callers whose actual repository token grants are read-only.
minimalChangeBoundary.writeCallers: Screenshots and image remain anonymous for dependency installation; preserve screenshot publishing and GHCR publishing permissions/steps.
minimalChangeBoundary.Docker: Remove automatic image writer-token submission; optional secret support may remain. No ARG, persisted ENV, new PAT, new identity or permission expansion.
notNeeded: No change to Native budget/window/first-pair measurement
No changes to server delta/home/SQL candidates
No parallel implementation by this reviewer

minimumProposed.boundary: Use the actual normal install lifecycle entry with a harmless allowed synthetic package/fixture. No optional input means the child sees no nonempty FFMPEG token. Emit only presence/equality booleans, never credential value.
An explicit synthetic read token reaches the intended normal installation path; it is not sourced from a separate generic GITHUB_TOKEN value.

Inspect actual screenshots and image job configs, including job-level permission overrides. They must not opt into shared action credential input or automatically send github.token as Docker secret. A small intentionally invalid configuration fixture must make this guard fail.
An explicitly reviewed read-token caller can opt in; keep existing release/OIDC responsibilities unchanged.

Retain anonymous download, exact API first-hop auth, redirect stripping, 30s/3redirect limits, complete bundle hashes and closed error diagnostics; successful install by itself is not the process-scope test.
